hook: The page you get may not be the page someone else gets: a banner at the top names the iteration you are viewing and tells you to reload after a minute for another. Each version is a short piece of fiction in which the characters end up reciting a containment file to each other. Try to read more than one if you can.
whyItMatters: It is a format experiment where the presentation itself is the anomaly. Instead of a report describing an entity that turns messages into stories, you only ever receive its stories, so the plain file never reaches you directly. That makes it a useful reference point for meta articles that put the reader inside the containment problem.
thingsToNotice:
In Iteration D the report is spoken as dialogue between Eleanor, dying of lung cancer in a hospital bed, and her wife Katherine, who feeds her the item number and object class like lines in a private game. The file itself explains the device: the original text survives intact as the characters' speech, while the setting and tone reflect the entity's mood and may shift depending on who is reading.

The menace stays at the edges here. A large man is waiting outside the room when Katherine arrives and is gone when she looks for help, and late on Eleanor hears something tapping down the hall like a bat being rolled along the floor. Then, just as she starts reading out the plan for terminating SCP-1893, she falls asleep for the last time, and the story ends with the termination method never spoken.
